thinking:
Both notebooks have similar structures, covering the basics of exploring a Dandiset. They both load the Dandiset using the DANDI API, load an NWB file, and visualize some data. However, Notebook 1 edges out Notebook 2 because it includes more visualizations and goes a little bit further in its exploration of the NWB file contents. The plot of electrode locations and spike raster plot enhance the understanding of the data and its structure, whereas Notebook 2 only shows the time series. Additionally, Notebook 1 provided a very basic listing of the contents of the NWB file, and Notebook 1 has a more detailed summary of the findings and discusses future analysis directions and potential use cases of this dataset.

However, both notebooks share some shortcomings:
- They both use remfile (which may not be necessary as direct download should work fine)
- They both load an arbitrary/unspecified time series (the notebooks should use some information present in the nwb file to make a better decision about what period of time to visualize)
- They both only scratch the surface of exploring the data (ideally they would read the paper associated with the dandiset and create some visualizations that relate to the actual experiment that was performed).

Given all these considerations, Notebook 1 is slightly better due to its more comprehensive exploration and additional visualizations.
